text_fidelity_a:
ACCUSPLIT AX740 PRO MEMORY (50) DUAL LINE STOPWATCH I often have three or 4 different workout groups going on at the same time and I have two of the older model 740MX watches and two of the newest AX740's to help me manage it all. What I like best about this watch is that after hitting the split button which I do at the beginning of every repeat in a set, I can hit the release button and the watch will show BOTH the Total Running Time AND the running repeat time. So if I am running a set of 100's on 1:20 I hit the split button at every 1:20, then hit the release button, it shows me the running repeat time so that I can eyeball the splits during the repeat and I can shout out times as they are coming in. It also shows the number of repeats so that I never lose count of the number of repeats. So with multiple groups and multiple watches it really helps me stay organized and allows me to give better feedback to the swimmers. I have had the two 740MX's for 10 years now and have used them nearly every day and often twice a day. Recently one or the other will blank out occassionally so I have purchased the newer AX740. I am not mentioning the blanking out as a problem but more of a testament that they have lasted this long under heavy use.

These are also wonderful watches for swim meets especially when you have the luxury of one watch per swimmer. Hit the split, write it down (or let the memory save it for later), hit release and see the total running time as well as the split running time.

If there is one drawback to this watch, it's that reset is made by holding down the start button for 2 seconds -- which seems like forever when you are trying to run a bunch of individuals doing one at a time 25's and you want to get ready for the next swimmer NOW. The older versions had a similar reset but it was about 1.3 seconds, the newer AX740 is a full 2 seconds. Sometimes I think my older watches are beginning to fail because I hold down the split button as hard as I can wishfulling thinking that it will speed up the reset. A light touch does the same and may lead to a longer life of the watch.
text_fidelity_b: ACCUSPLIT AX740 PRO MEMORY (50) DUAL LINE STOPWATCH

Zippo Champagne HeatBank 9s Rechargeable Hand Warmer When it comes to cold weather, sometimes it is hard to know how to prepare for the wide variety of temperatures where we live or travel. Having this hand warmer is very exciting. Let's see why..

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This hand warmer is a beautiful champagne color which is easy to find (as compared to black). There is a lanyard that you can use to keep it around your neck while camping or engaged in other activities. There is a recharge cord that plugs into a USB connection.

HEAT LEVELS
The heat levels vary. There are three blue lights- LOW MEDIUM AND HIGH but they indicate that BOTH sides of the hand warmer are warm. When you hit the heat button again, the green lights come on. That means only ONE side of the warmer is active and it also has low, medium, and high.

POWER BANK
This also serves as a power bank to recharge a tablet or cell phone. It can power a phone for an hour or two. I view it as being for emergency use only, however, due to the heavy draw on the unit.

HOW WELL DOES THIS WORK?
This works beautifully. As a hand warmer, it is fantastic. As a power bank, it is great for emergencies if you need to power your phone to make a quick call. The lanyard is perfect and allows me to keep this with me while hiking, camping or being at outdoor events.

HANDY
This has been very handy to have at games, camping, cold nights, and vacation. I love this.

RECHARGING
It takes about 3-4 hours to recharge this unit again.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For a fantastic handy device, this is great to have on hand for travels, outdoor activities or to bring in the car in the winter in case of a breakdown or emergency phone charge.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS! I love this and am VERY GLAD to have this. It has come in handy many times and having it this winter will be very exciting as I often have many opportunities where a hand warmer can help me through a tough spot. I highly recommend this unit especially if you engage in a lot of outdoor activities or live in an area with long winters or really cold weather seasons.
text_fidelity_b: Zippo Champagne HeatBank 9s Rechargeable Hand Warmer

Better yet, these pack up perfectly for anyone doing some outdoor camping and need to carry their own gear on foot to their destination.. Ha! Such a luxury once you set up camp!

The kaleidoscope design along with the zip around carrier makes this no bigger than a young girls church purse! The over the shoulder strap is also a bonus.. even your younger hikers could carry their own- it’s just too perfect!! The weight is the equivalent of carrying 2 disposable plastic water bottles- just to give you some perspective!

Once erect and locked into position this seat stays secure under the weight of even a large male adult without issue- I was shocked how sturdy this could actually be.. made of woven/interlocking plastic!!? And yet- it’s the woven structure that gives this it’s strength.. it’s such a novel concept- Pure wizardry!! When ready to put away- a simple “unlocking” twist allows for stool to collapse and zip closed.. The easiest part of camping by far!

These are great for seating but, they also make a solid makeshift table.. I loved the fact, they can be washed off so easily with water, rinsed with a hose.. dunked in a river- **I just recommend you let them dry completely before storing in the carrying case!

For any who find themselves needing a seat outdoors on the go.. camping, soccer game, or just a front yard seat around a fire pit- this delivers just as it says it will. Storing in a trunk is so easy.. with their tiny footprint you’ll never even know it’s there! I recommend without hesitation.. I hope this info can help your decision- happy adventures!

text_fidelity_a:
Becko 47 Inches Auto Open Umbrella Long Umbrella with 16 Ribs, Durable and Strong Enough for the Fierce Wind and Heavy Rain, Classic Style with Soft Foam Rubber Stick Handle, Unisex Umbrella This is an outstanding umbrella. I know it must sound silly to be so gushy about an umbrella, but I have never found a foldable umbrella that offered decent performance. This works just as well as my full-size umbrella with the huge benefit of being able to be folded up and carried in a briefcase.

The build quality is excellent, with well-made seams on the canopy, and very sturdy ribs. The automatic pop-up action is solid and quick to operate. The auto fold-up ability is equally well-done (e.g., you can push the “close” button and the canopy folds up, making it far easier to deal with once you’ve entered a building).

Wind resistance is quite good, with vent flaps that work well to prevent blowouts. The vents have a good amount of fabric overlap to keep any rain from getting through.

My only quibble is that it is hard to roll up so it fits back into the case. This canopy contains a lot of material and rolling/folding it up into a tight profile is a challenge. I didn’t have any problem folding it up enough to wrap it with the Velcro strap, but getting it to fit into the nylon pouch that it comes with is tough. I don’t consider that a negative since I never use those pouches, but point it out just in case that’s important to anyone who’s considering this.

Two huge (and dry) thumbs up for this umbrella. Great build quality, excellent performance, and compact when folded.
[Sample provided for review]

Stansport Aluminum Storage Capsule - Assorted 3-Pack Where many users of these tubes would select these for camping or taking along in wet environments, I have a completely different use for these - I selected them for geocaching. While they are, I was surprised by the size (even though the listing clearly states the sizes).

This is a set of three bison tubes, made of machined aluminum and fitted with a rubber gasket to create a water-tight seal when these are closed properly. The gasket also serves as a sort of lock washer and prevents each tube from easily unscrewing itself when jostled.

When sealed and submerged underwater for a length of time, these pass the waterproof test. Contents of each remained bone dry which is really one of the main points of a container like this.

The largest of these is sufficiently large to hold a writing utensil or a house key. I would hesitate to say it can hold a lot because, while it is a larger-than-average bison tube, it is not huge.

With the carabiners attached to these it is easy to snap these to a belt loop, bag strap or a tree branch.

I have found nothing about these that I find off-putting and I am pleased to recommend them if you need a water-tight and sturdy container (or set of containers) that can hold smaller items while protecting them. These seem to be made well and the cost is reasonable.

Rukket Sports Glow-Nana Inflatable Lounger, Blow Up & Light Up Air Chair & Couch for Lounging, Camping, Beach, & Festival, Sofa Hammock for Adults & Kids, LED Portable Wind Furniture Loungers This is a really cool product that once I figured out a few tricks to its use I’ve really enjoyed owning.

It will definitely help to watch videos on tips as to the best way to fill these loungers. If you’ve seen commercials showing people quickly swiping these through the air then sealing and sitting down - that is misleading. There must be enough airflow to adequately fill the lounger sack so that will require either a breeze or creating one. This can be accomplished by holding it open and running or, as I do, using a battery operated fan.

This product is different from others in this category as it has a pillow and a light built it with it - both are nice additions. In addition there are pouches on the side perfect for storing a drink, book, sunglasses, etc.

I got the “Glow Galaxy” model when the rechargeable battery powered light is illuminated the lounger glows a cool deep purple color illuminating the star pattern. During the day the light really isn’t noticeable but at night it’s incredible. The thing I’ve found I really like about having the light is when at a festival or on the beach it’s always easy to spot my group based on where my glowing lounger in located.

As with anything like this, air will slowly leak out - the more weight or pressure applied the faster air escapes. If someone drops too hard down on to it more air escapes. None of this is to be unexpected.

Sitting upright we fit 3 of us comfortably side by side although we are all relatively small.

While at first I wasn’t sure if I was going to figure out if I could fill this and seal it without the air escaping, now that I’ve used it for a while it’s really not a big deal. The lounger is comfortable, holds air adequately well and has nice design elements that others don’t. I have had multiple people stop to ask where I got it as it really is quite unique.

This is a cool product that I definitely recommend.
text_fidelity_b: Rukket Sports Glow-Nana Inflatable Lounger, Blow Up & Light Up Air Chair & Couch for Lounging, Camping, Beach, & Festival, Sofa Hammock for Adults & Kids, LED Portable Wind Furniture Loungers

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin vívofit 4 activity tracker with 1+ year battery life and color display. Large, Black. 010-01847-03 I love the app. It’s super user-friendly, and offers clear menus with your collected info, with options to connect with social media, plot running trails, and find popular places to walk/jog. If I were reviewing this solely on the app, this product would easily earn five stars,

BUT....

The data is 100% off. This is probably the most inaccurate fitness tracker I’ve used so far, both for step counts and sleep tracking. I used it for a little over a week to see if it could “learn”, or if different activities tracked more accurately, and it was pretty inconsistent.

Steps: I set a goal of 7,000 steps, which with my other trackers was a High goal. I could teach/take 3 hours of cardio-heavy dance and have regular activities other than that like cleaning up the house, doing office stuff, checking mail, etc, and I would *sometimes* get to 7,000. That’s Three Hours of cardio. Meanwhile, the last week has been full of house renovating, but that mostly consisted of staying in one place and repairing things, organizing things, and making runs to the hardware store. It did NOT consist of many steps or a bunch of walking. Even so, it said I made it to something around 9,000 steps. There is No Way I took that many steps. If I had to guess, I *maybe* made it to 5k. All week has been the same, with Very exaggerated counts.

Sleep: fail. More than half the nights, it showed no data at all and advised me to wear the band. I have literally not removed this thing even once in over a week, not even for showering. Other nights, it said I slept 8.5 hours, when I know I slept under four. I remembered the time I turned everything off and closed my eyes it was around 4am. I woke up around 8am. The phone said I was asleep by 11:30ish. Another night, it said I slept 10 hours, from 8pm-6-am. I can’t think of a time in the last decade that I’ve gone to bed at 8. I am practically a vampire. And that was on a day I finally got to sleep in, so I woke up at around 11. When I tried editing the data in hopes of teaching it, the system was buggy. I saved and exited the screen, and it went right back to the incorrect stuff. This would happen a few times, and in the end, I was only able to correct one of the nights successfully. I don’t have the energy to keep trying. Maybe it will get better, maybe not, but I’m not doing extra data entry work for this.

So all in all, I can’t recommend this product. The data is consistently wrong, which makes it practically impossible to assess what you’re doing or not doing.

Body Bar Power & Grace DVD This workout uses both a body bar and the gliding disks. Instructor Mindy Mylrea is joined by Keli Roberts, who modifies some of the exercises, and Violet Zaki, who increases the intensity.

Mylrea starts with a long (about 7 minutes) warm-up. During the warm-up, you are just holding the body bar and not really using it for resistance. In addition, she does not step on the disks until about halfway through the warm-up; at that time, she incorporates added moves such as twists plus side and back lunges.

For the standing portion of the workout, Mylrea takes greater advantage of the body bar. The option is often to hold the bar at the chest, on the shoulders, or overhead while performing classic strength moves such as side and front lunges, curtsey lunges, and deadlifts. The standing segment ends with push-up/plank work with the feet on the disks.

The floor work is shorter (18 minutes), but it continues to focus on the lower body with bridges and other moves targeting the hamstrings. Mylrea also includes abs work and a nice floor stretch (6 minutes), bringing in the entire workout right around 54 minutes.

I really enjoy Mylrea's original Gliding set, as I like mixing and matching from the 3 workouts on that DVD. For some reason, this workout didn't click as well with me, even though there aren't any major problems with the workout itself. One issue is that I do not have a body bar; substituting an unweighted stick and dumbbells worked okay, but this took some fun out of the workout. I also think that I have moved away from these type of cardio/strength circuit workouts now that I have discovered kettlebells.

For those who own both a body bar and gliding disks, however, I would recommend this DVD.
text_fidelity_b: Body Bar Power & Grace DVD

text_fidelity_a:
Sport Squad 2-in-1 Bean Bag/Cornhole and Ladder Toss Game Set for Indoor or Outdoor Use One thing my family loves is the ability to play lawn games. Bocce ball is a favorite around here as is badminton and a few other games we manage to get now and then. When I saw this game, I thought it would be perfect for our family. It would have been, had it not been broken upon arrival.

WHAT IS THIS SET LIKE?
First of all, this set is HEAVY. I mean HEAVY. That means if you have trouble lifting 50 lb bags of grain or similar type things, this might be a bit tough for you. It is doable, but challenging.

There are two score centers. Each one is folded up and they both come together back to back in a very tough canvas bag. The board centers are made of composite board( particle board?) and have a formica type top on them so that drops of water will bead up and not soak in. There is velcro on the pieces to hold them in place when using each different game and also for storage. The bars at the top for the ladder toss are metal and each one is color coded for scores

There are two rope handles one on each board. The idea is that you put the game boards in the case and the handles come through a hole in the top of the case for carrying. Carry pieces come in a mesh bag for the sand bags, and a plastic bag (we replaced with zipper close freezer bag) for the ladder toss pieces.

PLAYING PIECES
The playing pieces are sturdy and well made. There are three red and three blue heavy plastic balls joined by a tough nylon cord. You toss and they wrap around the ladder rungs if you score. There are also 4 blue and 4 red sand bags- not quite 3 inches square. The idea is that when the cornhole side of the board is up, you throw them in the hole.

GAME PLAY
The first way that you set up the game, there are two metal braces that you insert in holes in the frame of the ladder. The composite board (painted black on the back side) is on the grass or floor.

When you are ready to change the game, you unhook the ladder, flip it around and then brace it up in the back with a brace made of composite that props up the ladder underneath, thereby elevating the wood look board at an angle so you can throw the bags through the hole.

BROKEN
It is quite upsetting that a lot of effort went into this game, yet when it comes to the quality of the brace in the back to hold up the cornhole board, is horrible. It is very thin particle board (composite) and one of them came broken- it looked like it left the factory that way. We will try to fix it up by summer if it is possible, but such a horribly heavy game is way too difficult to send back in the mail/delivery. There should have been better quality control.

GAMEPLAY WITH ONE BOARD
We still played with the one board and the other propped up (although I really hate a new game being broken when you get it) and the gameplay was a lot of fun. We only played once outside as we got snow and it never left since. We played it in the basement, but it is more fun outside. We like to get as far away as we can to make it challenging.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For a simple lawn/basement game that will give loads of fun and hopefully stand up to some use if it is in proper shape when you get it, this is a lot of fun. We really enjoyed it. Unfortunately, despite the good quality work on most of the boards, the important brace is cheap and thin- this should have never been make like that. It is heavy to lift so make sure you have someone in the family or group who can lift heavy things to transport and set this up.

MY RATING
I took off two stars for the cheap broken brace. This never should have passed quality control. If this had been sturdier in the brace, I would have given it five stars. As it is, only three.
text_fidelity_b: Sport Squad 2-in-1 Bean Bag/Cornhole and Ladder Toss Game Set for Indoor or Outdoor Use

VSSL Supplies, Silver While I don't believe in Zombie apocalypse's, I do believe in Mother Nature and she's been known to throw a curve ball every now and then so being prepared for the unexpected is always wise. VSSL Supplies is a pre-loaded utility flashlight and basic survival kit in a 9" x 2" aircraft grade aluminum canister that weighs just 18 ounces, making it small and light enough to carry in a pack or in your vehicle when hiking, backpacking, or camping for a few hours or days.

The canister itself has a powerful 3 LED flashlight on the top that provides a bright light, a dimmer setting, and a setting that flashes SOS in international Morse code. The light is powered by 3 (included) E90 batteries, and the battery chamber requires a flat bladed tool such as a utility knife or a quarter to open, so you might want to tuck an extra E90 into three of the modules to have a spare set along and also tuck a quarter in one so you have the means to change batteries in the field.

The power button for the light protrudes a bit from the side of the cylinder which makes it easy to accidentally turn the light on, so you could stick a bit of tape over the top of one of the batteries or reverse the polarity of one of them until you need the light in order to conserve your battery life between use.

The bottom of the cylinder features a glow in the dark oil filled compass, so be careful when setting the tube down so you don't accidentally damage it. I got several false readings when using it while attached to the tube and found it to be more accurate when detached entirely and hand held. The cylinder itself is heavy enough when full to use as a defensive weapon, and it's also waterproof so you could remove the top, empty the contents out and use it to drink from.

The inside of the cylinder is stacked with well organized canisters carrying the various survival gear items, which include:

1. Instructions: Very basic and easy to understand, it uses icons to describe how to use the various items in the kit. Once you know how to use the items in the kit you can use this to help light a fire if necessary.

2. Can Opener & Aquatabs: You get one military style can opener plus a strip of water purification tablets (my kit had 10 of them), along with instructions on how many aquatabs to use with clear and unclear water. Depending on outside temperature and your activity level the average person requires between 2 - 3 liters of water per day, so there are enough tabs in the kit to keep you hydrated for a couple of days if you find a water source. These have an expiration date and are easy to replace when you need to.

3. Fishing Kit: Contains a pretty nice assortment of lures, swivels, jigs, sinkers, and 5# (or 6#) line. Use the hand held saw to cut a stick for a pole, catch some fish and you might not want to be rescued too soon.

4. Fire Starter & Mirror: This canister has a built in signal mirror, five flammable wicks, 10 waterproof matches, and a striker for the matches in the lid. I'd rather have has a magnesium fire starting kit, but that would be difficult to fit into the size of the tube.

5. Trail Markers & Whistle: Contains a decent quantity of pre-fashioned white and red reflective trail markers and a loud whistle to call for help with.

6. Beeswax Candle: Rated as a 4 hour candle, this provides light, could be used in lieu of matches to start or keep your fire going, and can provide you with some heat as well.

7. Rope & Razor Blade: A spool holding 20' of marine grade rope with 250lb breaking strength along with a standard razor blade to cut it with. This is useful for making splints, setting up snares, lashing poles to form a travois, lashing branches to build a shelter, and a plethora of other uses.

8. Wire Saw: This is a sturdy feeling braided wire saw with nylon loops you can hold onto that you can use to cut branches for a fire or to build a shelter with. As you finish a cut be sure to cut away from yourself so you don't accidentally cut yourself.

9. First Aid: The supplies in this module are the least useful in my opinion. When I think of the types of injuries most likely to occur to a hiker, backpacker, camper, or anyone in the outdoors, the main things to come to mind are sprains, broken bones, stings, burns, abrasions, and lacerations. This kit is designed to handle minor cuts only. It contains a generic OTC pain pill, several alcohol wipes, a bit of neosporin, several butterfly closures, several standard size bandages, and one medium size knee or elbow pad, several safety pins and a roll of medical tape.

There is nothing to apply pressure with to stop large bleeds, nothing to help clot a wound, no burn ointment or dressings, and no triangular bandage to use for a sprain or to make a sling with, so I'm not clear on what they intended people to use the tape or safety pins for. I will probably get rid of the tape and some of the other stuff and replace them with a few other things.

One nice thing about these modules is that they can be customized as long as you can get stuff that fits into them. This VSSL Supplies Survival Kit is expensive, and there's no doubt that someone who knows what they need to build an all around survival kit could source their own items and put a kit together that doesn't cost as much as this does.

Most people don't already know what they would need to survive on their own in the outdoors if they were injured or caught in weather and couldn't make it back home for a few days though. This survival kit is lightweight, small enough to toss in a glove box or backpack, and contains the basics a person would need in order to stay alive in an emergency, so despite it's price, I do think it's a good item to take along when you're camping, backpacking, hiking, or even to keep in the car.

Retail sample provided at no cost by manufacturer for evaluation purposes.
text_fidelity_b: VSSL Supplies, Silver

STAR BRITE Ultimate Citrus Cleaner & Degreaser - 32 OZ (096432) I went outside this morning to find that a vulture had strafed our new Honda CRV. One of the many hazards in Southwest Florida is the abundance of bird droppings from several relatively large species, with the vultures and pelicans giving the most bang for the buck. Sometimes I swear that these birds know when you have a new car in the driveway.

I always spray the offended area with a mist from our hose and let it sit for about a minute to help break up the chalky residue from bird poop. Afterwards you can apply a quick shot of any good quality cleaner and degreaser, let it soak in for another minute, and then wipe away gently with a clean cloth.

This Star Brite works well on this particular problem but I wouldn't categorize the product as being "ultimate". However I was pleasantly surprised when I used it to clean the burned on grease on our countertop burners. It was just a simple matter of spraying a bit on, letting it sit for a bit, and then scraping the residue off with a razorblade.

The only thing that I have found that works better cleaning cooktops is the Cerama Bryte Complete Cooktop Cleaning Kit which sells for about $2.00 more for the kit. However the Cerama Bryte cleaner is less useful on other projects around the house. The Star Brite smells better and gives you 32 oz. of a more 'all purpose' formula to use.
text_fidelity_b: STAR BRITE Ultimate Citrus Cleaner & Degreaser - 32 OZ (096432)

text_fidelity_a:
Arccos Driver Golf GPS Shot Tracker Just a nice weighless device that you put onto your driver, pair with the app on your smart phone, and that's it, it's ready to go.

The application is easy to use. The Arccos app has the information for a number of courses worldwide. I can't say that they are all accurate, can only say it was very accurate for the course I was golfing on today.
Plus it uses GPS to map exactly where you are.

If you're into fun competition, you can share your information with friends for additional competition.
This is a nice device for monitoring your golf driving stats.
There is a summary screen that shows your smart distance, the number of fairway hits, your smart range, longest drive, and your driver handicap.

I am only a recreational player that can only get out a few times a month. So this is just a fun toy for me. I've never tried any other type of GPS tracking devices for golfing so I can't compare the Arccos sensor to any others that are out on the market.
Best to keep your phone in your pocket when you play. You could lose bluetooth connection if you leave it in your bag.

I guess you can purchase a premium subscription but, I couldn't find any information about it. But then again I didn't do any big time researching because it's not anything I would be interested in.
Would be nice if they sold a set for all the clubs. Would be nice to be able to analyze my entire game instead of just the holes where I use my driver.

I'll enjoy using this as an avid golfer. I'm sure the ones that get out and golf more will get full use of all the features that this device has.
text_fidelity_b: Arccos Driver Golf GPS Shot Tracker

text_fidelity_a:
LifeSpan TR200 Compact Treadmill *************** Following is an update to my original review:
It is now June 25, 2012. I've lowered my review to three stars instead of five. After about 1 month of use an intermittent, irritating rattle started in the back of the machine by the bumpers. Its not so bad that it warrants someone to come and repair it because the machine still functions, plus the rattle is intermittent. I've emailed the company and they sent me a service manual. I've tried to understand it and take the back bumpers off to look inside but the instructions are not very clear on how to do that. Plus, I do not know how to read schematics and I don't want to get too adventurous and screw something up.

Its not possible to speak to anyone in person at that company. All communication with customer service is by email. I wanted to show someone how the treadmill sounds, which of course I can't do my email. So, I'm stuck with the rattle. There is no way I'm going to pay to send it back.

My original review:

I've been using this machine for strenuous walking for about 3 weeks and I am very pleased. It is remarkably quiet, which I need in my apartment. And it folds up much smaller that others I've seen. The only thing I don't like is that the cord could be a little longer. I prefer to be facing into the room, not the wall, and the cord is a little too short to be able to do that without butting the machine right up against the wall. But a shord extension cord solved the problem. The shipping company, CEVA, delivered it right on schedule and the box was not damaged and they gave me notice when the box would be delivered. I highly recommend the treadmill and the shipping company.
text_fidelity_b: LifeSpan TR200 Compact Treadmill

text_fidelity_a:
Klymit Insulated Static V Luxe Inflatable Sleeping Pad for Camping, Lightweight Hiking and Backpacking Air Bed For Cold Weather, 3 Inch Thick I've previously owned a Klymit V without the "Luxe," but a piece of the one valve it had broke off in short order. This Klymit V Luxe has valves which *appear* to me to have fewer fiddly parts, and there are two of them--more on why that's good in a moment!

First off, these pads have a smart design. Although there is no railing per say, the Vs help to keep you on them which is good news if you do not stay in one place on a bed. The material keeps the air inside from feeling cold (and presumably from drinking in too much of the earth's cold).

The primary use I gave my original V was as a buffer between me and an extremely ill-suited new mattress while I desperately shopped for solutions. And although I've been a backpacker in the past, sadly, my primary intended use for the Static V Luxe is to act as a buffering layer when I need to sleep on other people's mattresses. I have considerable back health issues, and this padding is incredibly helpful for when I cannot be on my own mattress. I purchased this size this time because the original V is so much smaller than a twin bed that it was downright silly trying to use it for my purpose. Also I use a body pillow and change positions a lot. This will clearly be nicer for managing nights out of my own bed.

Now I saw someone complaining about the two valves because they are confusing. This person has probably never experienced the downsides of only having one valve for letting air out of a mattress. Sure, you need to be certain that the valve you are not blowing into is closed so that the mattress can properly inflate, but oh, my word, it is soooooo much easier to get the air out of this mattress pad! I could almost never get my original V small enough to properly stick into its dry sack. But this larger V luxe easily packs up smaller than I could get the original V to go. Ok, so maybe "easy" is relative. You do need to open both valves, roll it down from bottom to top, open it up again, fold a few times, and roll once more to get it maximally small. But it actually works and stuffs in the drysack.

I hope if you're reading this that you have more adventurous uses afoot, but I do recommend this Static V Luxe and wish I'd had one back when I was a backpacker!
text_fidelity_b: Klymit Insulated Static V Luxe Inflatable Sleeping Pad for Camping, Lightweight Hiking and Backpacking Air Bed For Cold Weather, 3 Inch Thick

text_fidelity_a:
MODZ® Flip4 Club Car DS Golf Cart Rear Seat Kit – White You bought a golf cart, but you need that rear seat. You see this listing on Amazon and can't wait for it to arrive. The good news is that it arrives fairly quickly and in pristine packaging, excellent. There are 2 boxes, one has the structural components, the other has the pads... sure.
You open box 1 for all of the structural components to be laid out and to get your project started. No sense getting the seat pads dirty so you leave box 2 sealed up. After separately out the somewhat accurately described bolt kit labels, you decide to get started. Removing the old pieces from your cart is somewhat of a detailed process and is mostly accurate. DO save all of those pieces just in case (pro tip, there will be a just in case).
You've got the cart in the state it needs to be to begin your assembly. As you begin to use the available bolts you start to loosely piece this thing together so sooner or later it looks like a cart seat. The problem here is that several bolts are not found, you need to open box 2 to find those because they are in there when it was close to 5 o'clock on a Friday and that box wasn't sealed before heading out the door at the Modz warehouse.
Anyways, you've now probably got all your nuts and bolts for the cart and a few have loosened up inside your head trying to figure this out. Most of the pieces will line up properly, though attaching the post to the old seat back slot might not work because they weren't fully drilled out like mine. This is where the old bolts come into play (that's not on Modz though).
You are loosely assembling most of the pieces only to find out that the bolts they provided are kind of accurately labeled for proper measurements. It would've been better to just use a metric ruler though because some bolts ended up where they didn't below. The good news is that you've got some extra bolts you didn't use because you used some of the old bolts. Unfortunately, those are the shortest bolts of the kit so you can't use them anyways. Now you've got some sick spare bolts for some future project that may or may not require them.
Once you go to attach the arm rest to the base of the cart you realize the available bolts will be too long so you can't properly open up the seat to turn into a flat bed. This is where the extra washers come into play (don't worry there's somewhere between 10-67 extra washers) so you can shore up the bolt head so there's less available thread on the end. This helps make sure that the bed opens up properly because you are about ready to lay down anyways. The rest of the assembly goes fairly smooth, though getting the seat back supports off the old Club Car DS is super fun since the nut is buried inside of a channel where only a small team of your kids' GI Joe's tools could fit. Once you've turned into Superman to bend that aluminum enough to gap and get the bolt head secure and the incredibly precise angle of your pliers to free up that seatback support you are home free.
From there it's only a few more screws before you are done with a project that you estimated to take about 45 minutes lasted nearly 3 hours.
Cheers! Next time we get to install turn signals, that'll be easy...
text_fidelity_b: MODZ® Flip4 Club Car DS Golf Cart Rear Seat Kit – White

text_fidelity_a:
Coleman Pack Away LED Mini Lantern (Colors May Vary) I purchased the [[ASIN:B0018S4XIS Rayovac Sportsman LED Lantern (SE3DLNA)]] and this Coleman mini lantern. Both are bright but this pack away mini is great for when I need a little less light or want to carry a lantern that performs almost as well as the Rayovac but in a lot smaller package. For instance, this would be great to carry when walking outside in the dark because it's very light (about 8 ounces) and bright and makes a person visible enough to be seen.

What I like about this lantern is:
- It takes 4 AA batteries instead of the "highly in demand" D batteries that most flashlights use.
- The mini lantern fits in the palm of my hand when I collapse the LED portion into the unit.
- Mine came with a mini carabiner that I could hook onto the handle for easy carrying on a pant belt loop or backpack.
- The bottom battery compartment screws out by hand by turning the plastic grip several times until the cap came off.
- There are three modes of high, low, and strobe. The low mode does not look low to me and seems very similar to high but it's supposed to save battery life. Just pressing and releasing the top black button changes the mode.
- When the unit is collapsed, the light cannot accidentally be turned on which is a great feature.
- The unit is relatively light compared to full-sized lanterns.
- The package claims the LED lasts a lifetime and never has to be changed.

I purchased this at WallMart for $19.99 plus tax ($21.39) which is $1.60 less than Amazon's current price of $22.99.

This mini lantern suits me for small jobs and lights up my bathroom or kitchen with enough light to see without being blinding. In summary, there isn't anything I don't like about this lantern.
text_fidelity_b: Coleman Pack Away LED Mini Lantern (Colors May Vary)

text_fidelity_a:
Gaiam Keep Your Cool Yoga Kit I am regular yoga practitioner who has also been a teacher for about two years now, and I have tried a LOT of yoga mats! I have given many away and still own several. I prefer a mat that is not too thick, more dense than squishy, but most important of all, is non-slip, ESPECIALLY when my hands are on the mat, such as in downward facing dog. I was attracted to the mandala pattern on this mat and thought it would be great to keep at work, where I teach a weekly noontime yoga class.

When the mat arrived, I was actually a bit disappointed in the appearance, which more brightly colored and garish than the photo would suggest. I thought that it was a green design on gray, but it is actually a navy blue background and looks quite "busy," especially on the water bottle. I will say that others have complimented me on it, so I guess it's just me. The mat did have an odor that I've found with many other new mats and that I tend to think of as a "pool toy plastic" scent. After laying it out and using it a few times, this has dissipated, and I haven't really noticed it.

I have been satisfied with the performance of the mat. It is thick (6mm) but NOT squishy, which is important to me. And I have NOT found it to be slippery under my hands, which is also key. However, I wouldn't recommend using this mat for travel, as the thickness makes it quite heavy. It is so large when rolled that even though it is a Gaiam-brand mat, it did not fit into my Gaiam-brand mat tote! ([[ASIN:B01N6UECXE Gaiam All Day Yoga Tote, Grey]]) Overall, this is a very good mat, depending on how you want to use it.
text_fidelity_b: Gaiam Keep Your Cool Yoga Kit

text_fidelity_a:
Lockdown Gun Concealment Magnet , Black The Lockdown Gun Magnet is almost... almost what I needed.

It has the two thicker discs, connected by ferrous metal, with a soft rubber coating. The magnetism is on the logo'd side; it won't even hold itself up against a fridge on the other side. So make sure you mount it correct-side-out.

It seems nicely made and equipped. The rubber is non-scuffing and won't hurt the guns. The screw-holes are counter-sunk. It comes with drywall anchors and three lengths of black screws. (The packaging claims two sets of screws.) Both sides of it are rubber-coated, so no rattles or vibrations. The first impressions are great.

It is decently strong; it can lift a 5-pound weight disk. But that's a pretty perfect case; flat metal, smooth, full contact, being lifted straight up. And it isn't a strong grip on the 5-pound disk; you can shake it loose pretty easily.

And that's the problem. A typical handgun (e.g. Star Firestar - 2#, Browning Hi-Power 2.3#, Colt 1911 2.5#) weighs about half that weight disk... but it doesn't have all the metal on the surface and doesn't have a smooth flat contact patch. So the Lockdown doesn't hold a typical handgun tightly enough for the odd placement and motion in a vehicle. In fairness, the Kahr PM9 is about 1.3 # loaded, the Beretta Nano 9mm about 1.1# loaded and the Colt Mustang Pocketlite .380 and Beretta Pico .380 barely 3/4-pound, but they also have less ferrous metal in them for the magnets to grip.
text_fidelity_b: Lockdown Gun Concealment Magnet , Black

I'm using these on 2 bikes, and have attached them to traditional round-spoke wheels as well as wheels with flat/"bladed" spokes, and they fit both and stay on (haven't had one fly off yet). These use different (smaller, CR927) batteries than some other Nite Ize lights, and I haven't used them enough to rate battery life yet. I got these mainly because the Spoke Lit model had a habit of getting loose and banging against the fork.

Good Stuff:
-smaller than other spoke lights; haven't had problems with them rubbing the fork, brakes, etc. on mountain or road bike
-seem to stay in-place a bit better than the Spoke Lit model (at least one they're positioned correctly); these fasten with a clip instead of just a press-fit
-lighter than the older Spoke Lit model

Bad Stuff:
-not as bright; will be visible, but if you want a lot of wattage on the wheel, may need to double-up
-only light the wheel in one direction; thus, a pack of 2 would cover 1 wheel
-no blink mode; just solid-on or solid-off

text_fidelity_a:
Ringside Pro Style IMF Tech Boxing Training Sparring Gloves We just purchased a super tall, somewhat more slender than usual cylindrical punching bag from the same brand, and so were looking for a good set of starter punching gloves that would allow us to have fun with our new fitness toy. In the past, I've had a brand of punching gloves (which I brought with me to the gym) that I didn't like so much, because there was an uncomfortable seam that hit right about where my fingernails were, so every time I would get punching, a few minutes in and my fingertips would start feeling a little sore and bruised. Yet I didn't want to spend a great deal of money on something that would only be used for probably 30 minutes a day at most.

So I was very excited to be offered this set of 18 ounce midrange punching gloves for review, because they seemed like the perfect middle-of-the-road option. Indeed, not only do these fit my size small women's hands, but they also fit my husband's hands comfortably, and he usually wears a size medium to large. If you have very large hands, you might find these a little tight, but for the size hands that we have, and the fact that we were hoping to be able to share them despite having a pretty big difference in our hand size, these are perfect.

The material and stitching seem high quality, and I like the fit, which is compressive enough that they do not slide around yet not so tight that either of us feels our circulation is being cut off. The seaming is perfect, and there are no places where seam falls in an awkward or uncomfortable place on my hands. I like that the material over the hand is matte rather than shiny, as the shiny material on my last one sometimes had an effect on how the glove slid, or didn't, across the punching bag.

The molded foam provides good protection, and overall these are such a huge notch nicer than the ones that were half the price that I would expect them to be priced higher than they are. While I have never personally gotten to try the more expensive ones made for people who are more serious about MMA or boxing, for people who enjoy just a casual work out with the punching bag, I think these are the nicest ones you could possibly need. We've been super impressed by them.
text_fidelity_b: Ringside Pro Style IMF Tech Boxing Training Sparring Gloves

text_fidelity_a:
Sportline Lightweight Walking Advantage 385 Tally Counter With Easy To Read Number Display That Counts Up To 9999 Anyone working out on an indoor track will find a counter helpful. At 12 laps a mile, counting laps is difficult. Counting is easy; remembering how many laps I've done is hard.

The Sportline counter fixes what my math teacher could not, allowing me to turn my mental energies toward my workout, or toward a conversation with my running partner.

---Necessary on a Practical Level---
I tried a system of using my fingers on my right hand to measure laps 1-5, then using my left hand to measure how many laps in groups of five. That is, two fingers on my left and three fingers on my right would equal 13 laps. It sounds easier to employ than it actually is.

The Sportline counter has five worthwhile features:
* It counts one per click, up to 9,999. I won't run more than that, so, for me, it is plenty.
* The display is legible while running. The white digits are large, on a black background.
* The size of the device is small enough to carry.
* The finger loop fits nicely in my middle finger.
* The reset dial quickly zeroes out the counter.

The only two drawbacks are
* The reset dial would be more comfortably located on the left, not the right side of the counter, or otherwise better engineered for right-handed users.
* The weight is heavy. It is small, but can feel like baggage during a longer workout.

The Sportline counter is sturdy, does as advertised, and serves well as a tool for anyone walking or running a lot of laps.

Anthony Trendl
[...]
text_fidelity_b: Sportline Lightweight Walking Advantage 385 Tally Counter With Easy To Read Number Display That Counts Up To 9999

text_fidelity_a:
Withings ActivitÃ Steel - Activity and Sleep Tracking Watch I had high hopes for this device. I think it's aimed at people who don't want a gadget to play with, but a useful and attractive minimalist activity tracker. It qualifies as attractive and, if all you want to do is count steps, it is useful. Ultimately, I had to quit wearing it because it caused a severe rash on my wrist under one side of the band. I have reached out to Withings and I will update this review when my issue is resolved (or not). At this point I just want to return it for the following reasons:

1. The rash was severe. I've now gone 2 weeks without wearing the watch and it has barely diminished. I'm not allergic to silicone, so I wonder what chemicals are in or on the band.
2. The lack of contrast between the hands and the face result in a watch I can only read in good light. In a dimly lit room it is completely unreadable.
3. A big reason the watch appealed to me is that I can wear it while swimming. It is supposed to log swim time, but it was unreliable to the point of being useless for this purpose.
4. I was intrigued by the sleep tracking, but it has quirks that make me doubt it's usefulness. For example, if I sit on the couch reading or watching TV for an hour before bed, sometimes it logs this as sleep, including deep sleep.

The watch counts from 50% to 20% less steps than my Samsung app. I can't say which is more accurate. I like the idea of an elegant and simple tracker/watch, and this was almost it. Ultimately nothing else matters because I can't wear it. The negatives add up to the point that I'm not interested in resolving the rash problem with a different band.

Update: I reached out to Withings. They responded quickly and seemed genuinely concerned. They dealt with my problem promptly and fairly. I'm upping my review from 2 stars to 3 stars because of the customer service.
text_fidelity_b: Withings ActivitÃ Steel - Activity and Sleep Tracking Watch

text_fidelity_a: Schwinn Sport or Cruiser Comfort Bike Seat Cover, High-Tech Gel or Memory Foam Cushion Padded Saddle Covers, Fits Most Bicycle I have a Spinner brand Spinbike with a narrow, hard-as-a-rock seat and decided to get this seat pad in hopes a more comfortable ride would entice me to ride more. The seat cover isn't as wide and bulky as it looked in the photo. It might not work on an extra wide beach cruiser type seats but for regular and narrow it should be fine. It slips over the seat and a string and toggle are used to  cinch it tight.  If using this on an outdoor bike you will probably need or want to cut the strings shorter or maybe tie a bow once it's fastened on.  I was kind of concerned that this would be a little slippery because the material is slick but I haven't had a problem staying on the seat when spinning quickly.  I would also like to note that when I ride I do not usually wear cycling or work-out shorts and the shorts I do wear have seams in them so before I got this seatcover I was experiencing quite a bit of discomfort,  but I don't want to have to go in and change my clothes to exercise because it's just another excuse to not do it.  My first ride when I received the seat cover was just over 30 minutes and I was wearing a pair of cargo shorts. I had very little to no discomfort while riding and even the next day I only noticed the slightest hint when riding again. I am very pleased with this seat cover. text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Basics Strap-On Wedge Saddle Bag for Cycling The saddle bag is a decent, basic product that suits its purpose. Here are some specific points:
Size: You have the dimensions, so you know the size. It’s tapered from top to bottom, so that’s something to consider beyond just the dimensions. It’s not a commuter bag—not its intent—and so its size is more than suitable I’d say for those little things you might want to carry with you on a ride: you phone, keys, whatever you carry money in (for those who still carry money). You can fit a tube and tool set in for peace of mind, but that will obviously reduce room for those other things depending on their size.

Form: as mentioned, it’s tapered toward the bottom so it fits against the bike under the seat. It’s pretty long, so you’ll want to make sure it will fit under the seat—I can see some bikes not having space for it depending on how high their seat is raised (mine is just on the edge of this being a good fit). Same is true if you have a rack over your back wheel (for panniers)—it’s so long that there’s a decent chance it will overlap the rear part of the rack. It is flexible enough to crunch down and reduce its footprint, but obviously then you’ve ust lost some of its total space.

There’s a small mesh pocket inside to keep something separate (in other words so it doesn’t just mix in the large space, making it easier for instance to grab your keys instead of fishing around). It’s a decent solution but I would have preferred if it had also zipped.

Construction: it seems solidly built enough. The material appears pretty tough, as if it will handle wear and tear well, along with the elements. I’m not sure about how it will do with rain (at least not yet). I don’t get a sense (and there was no documentation) that it is water “proof”, but my guess would be it is at least somewhat water “resistant” based on the feel and construction of the material. Personally, until you’ve experienced a good rainfall (we’re in drought conditions here) and can see how it deals, I’d put anything valuable in a plastic bag.

Mounting: Simple and easy. Three straps/loops that give it good stability. Thanks to the three straps and the size, it doesn’t move/shift around at all under my seat.

So a nice little carry-on but definitely check that the length will work for you (especially people with their seat pretty low).
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics Strap-On Wedge Saddle Bag for Cycling

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit One Wireless Activity Plus Sleep Tracker, Burgundy I just received the Fitbit One yesterday, so I can't really give as detailed a report as some of the others I've read. I spent a very long time deciding which item to purchase - did I want a Flex? Did I want my heart rate monitored? I think the first thing to figure out is what you exactly want to accomplish.

For my needs, tracking my steps, calories burned and sleep is really what I wanted and the Fitbit One had outstanding ratings. As well, I did not want to have to wear anything on my wrist during the day. The clip vs. band was a huge plus for me. Plus the burgundy color is really nice (though where I clip it, no one sees it anyway).

I downloaded the free Fitbit app and created an account online as soon as I got it (you have to activate and set up online anyway). It asks for your goals as far as weight loss, in what time frame, steps per day goals, etc. You can make changes if you need to. Based on the goals you set for your weight loss amount and how hard you are willing to work for it (from easy at 0.5 lbs/week to very hard at 2 lbs/week), it will calculate how many calories a day you should be eating and then tell you how long it should take to reach your goal. This is the website or app, not the Fitbit One itself.

The Fitbit is small and I barely notice I'm wearing it. The clip is a rubbery material that is very soft, so it is easy to get the One into and out of the clip when you want to put it into the band for sleeping. I clip it to clothes on my upper body as per the instruction recommendations, and I don't remember it is there. You can set a message for when you first start it up, and then you can cycle through various stats, like # steps walked, stairs climbed, miles walked, calories burned, and then it will show the time all on the display.

On the website/app, you will get more details about all the areas that are tracked. When you meet a milestone, it has a little "hooray" for you - for example today I met my steps goal.

If you want it to track your sleep, you need to put it in the sleep band. I did that last night and it is super easy to get the One out of the clip and slip it into the band. I had to keep the band fairly loose so it wouldn't be uncomfortable - it isn't the softest material - but when I fell asleep I didn't even notice I had it on. In the morning, it gave me details about my sleep pattern and how long I was actually sleeping vs. how long I was in bed, which I think is super helpful.

This is a great tool, but like any tool the responsibility is still on the individual. You have to manually enter your food in the online tracker (or in the app), and it will tell you how many calories you've eaten, how many you have left, etc. It will also tell you how many you may have left because of the amount of calories you've burned. But that is all dependent on a person taking the time to put the information in and doing so accurately. For me, that's the hardest part (I've tried food tracker apps in the past). I think once I get into the habit and make it my routine, it shouldn't be so difficult.

Synching data from the One to the computer/app is done wirelessly. I noticed it makes it to my app (via bluetooth) much more quickly than it makes it to my computer. Sometimes I have to refresh the computer several times to get it to show the right number of steps, etc. However, there is so much more information in the online dashboard than in the app, and you can get into great detail about your sleep and other things that I really do want it to synch accurately (and quickly) with my computer.

My one complaint is that I didn't realize it already came with a clip and a sleep band so I bought them separately. That might be MY mistake, though, so I didn't take any stars off for it. But if you want to buy this, unless you want to have an extra clip and band just in case, you do NOT need to buy them separately.

Overall, I'm very pleased with this choice. It was a tough decision but so far so good.

I'll update if status after I've used it for awhile.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit One Wireless Activity Plus Sleep Tracker, Burgundy

text_fidelity_a:
Sportline 385 Digital Tally Counter (Chrome) Anyone working out on an indoor track will find a counter helpful. At 12 laps a mile, counting laps is difficult. Counting is easy; remembering how many laps I've done is hard.

The Sportline counter fixes what my math teacher could not, allowing me to turn my mental energies toward my workout, or toward a conversation with my running partner.

---Necessary on a Practical Level---
I tried a system of using my fingers on my right hand to measure laps 1-5, then using my left hand to measure how many laps in groups of five. That is, two fingers on my left and three fingers on my right would equal 13 laps. It sounds easier to employ than it actually is.

The Sportline counter has five worthwhile features:
* It counts one per click, up to 9,999. I won't run more than that, so, for me, it is plenty.
* The display is legible while running. The white digits are large, on a black background.
* The size of the device is small enough to carry.
* The finger loop fits nicely in my middle finger.
* The reset dial quickly zeroes out the counter.

The only two drawbacks are
* The reset dial would be more comfortably located on the left, not the right side of the counter, or otherwise better engineered for right-handed users.
* The weight is heavy. It is small, but can feel like baggage during a longer workout.

The Sportline counter is sturdy, does as advertised, and serves well as a tool for anyone walking or running a lot of laps.

Anthony Trendl
editor, HungarianBookstore.com
text_fidelity_b: Sportline 385 Digital Tally Counter (Chrome)

text_fidelity_a:
humangear CapCAP+ | Converts Wide-Mouth Openings | Secure Easy Open | Food-Safe Material I have put this cap through about 1 months’ worth of daily heavy use, and have no complaints so far. Unfortunately for me, I have pissed away a lot of money searching for a suitable cap, so I am writing this review so maybe someone else won’t have to go through that. These are the caps that I have tried:

Hydro Flask Wide Mouth Flip Lid + Jug Lug for a whopping total of $10.50
Very poor water flow. It turns a quick gulp of water into a time consuming chore. The jug lug sits under the cap loose, so there is another thing that can fall to the ground when re-loading with ice water

Camelbak Durable Chute Cap $7.00
This lid fits the Hydro Flask leak-free as long as you remove the cap retainer strap. Problem is the spout cap started not seating properly and leaking after about 2 weeks’ worth of use.

Humangear Capcap $6.00
Fits the Hydro Flask leak-free with no modifications what-so-ever. Quickly and easily get a nice guzzle of water. The drinking spout retainer strap doubles as a handle for lugging the flask around. Another reviewer indicated that they really stand behind their product, which really makes the capcap a winner! I will update this review if the capcap starts to fail; however, I hope that never happens.

***Update***
It is now 3/23/2017. After 1.5 years of daily / nightly, take with me everywhere use, the capcap is still holding up leak free on my HydroFlask, and still facilitating nice guzzles of water.

Most of the time I finish my water long before the ice has melted in my HydroFlask, so I am able to refill water thru the top cap easy.

This is ice-water Utopia people. Waking up in the middle of the night for fast slam of cold ice water, has never been easier or more pleasurable for me.

8/17/2018 Update:

Same cap still going strong. Price has went up a little bit since my first review, but provided they don't take the low road and cheapen the product up, it's still a pretty good value.

In fact, this same cap is on it's second Hydro Flask now. My brown one failed, and was replaced with a cobalt one under warranty, since they no longer make the brown. TMy Capcap however, is no worse for the wear apart from some scuffs. I suspect I'll be screwing it onto my 3rd Hydro Flask someday...
text_fidelity_b: humangear CapCAP+ | Converts Wide-Mouth Openings | Secure Easy Open | Food-Safe Material

text_fidelity_a:
Coleman Trailhead II Cot Purchased this cot for a week long camping trip. Set it up in my house to make sure it wasn’t defective or missing parts. Everything was in working order!

Pros: Sturdy, wide enough for the camping pads we have, will get us off the ground and serve its purpose for my week long trip.

Cons: Pretty heavy and the bag hardly holds it. Definitely for car camping with a short walk from the car. Hard to assemble and disassemble. So would only use it on longer trips because otherwise I wouldn’t want to bother with it.

Note: I definitely recommend watching videos on how to assemble it. The 2nd tension bar is very difficult to put on and remove and I found a video where the guy recommended putting it on its end and using your foot to put in the last tension bar. This was the only way I could assemble it. After learning this technique I’m confident I’ll be able to do this by myself. Just a little worried about having to do wrestle with it in the heat after lugging all my gear.

Edit after using: Worked great on my trip, but had to assemble and disassemble it outside of my tent because of how difficult it is to assemble, which isn’t ideal and the process really added stress to setup and breakdown of everything. Loved cot camping but don’t like how heavy and difficult this cot was to setup, so I plan on doing more research for a lighter and easier to setup cot and willing to spend more for these features.
text_fidelity_b: Coleman Trailhead II Cot
